utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. Case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to greet everyone present, members of the Prosecution, almost all present; Defence counsel; the accused; and the witness who is now in the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters request counsel to please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: The summary of the statement of Witness CE. The witness lived in Stolac town until 1993 and worked at the Kostana hospital. In May, 1993, the HVO took over Kostana hospital in Stolac town and evacuated the patients to the Grabovina barracks without any medical support. The witness herself got a summons to go for work to Grabovina but did not comply with them. The witness learned that the patients were treated as prisoners at Grabovina. After the evacuation, the HVO used Kostana hospital for gathering prisoners and for torture. Later in May, 1993, the witness was arrested and taken to the MUP building for questioning. Upon release, she hid, but was again arrested later, interrogated, and placed in an isolation cell. In June/July, 1993, all Muslim men in fighting age in Stolac were systematically arrested by the HVO. Houses were searched. Boys and elderly people were also arrested. On the 4th of August, 1993, all Muslim civilians were expelled from Stolac town. The witness and others were ordered by the HVO soldiers to leave the keys of their houses in the doors. The witness, together with hundreds of other civilians, was escorted by HVO soldiers to the TGA factory where they were searched and stripped of their possessions. Muslim civilians were forced into trucks and shipped to Capljina. The witness and her mother were taken to Crnici primary school. Other Muslims from the Dubrava plateau were already held there. The witness and the other civilians were held in squalid conditions. On the 14th of August, 1993, the witness moved to the VPD building where she had to sleep on the ground. There was only one toilet for 40 people. The witness was interrogated three times. One of her co-detainees fell ill and died. On the 2nd of October, 1993, the HVO sent the sick and the elderly to Blagaj. Two people died on the way. On the 19th of November, 1993, the witness was herself expelled from Buna to Blagaj. This, Your Honours, is the summary of the statement of Witness CE.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness CE, when you provided your statement to the investigator, did you do so truthfully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do so freely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the conclusion of the interview, your statement was read back to you, wasn't it, in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown the Exhibit number 9750, 9750. That is the statement in the French language, which is the original. I think the usher has a bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me when you believe it's necessary to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I believe that the witness is looking at the B/C/S version. I would like her to look at the original version. Maybe we can put it on the screen on e-court. And can I ask the Court to move into private session and have this document shown because it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you had to give a statement today before this Court, would the content of at that statement be the same as what is in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like now to go to some exhibits to be shown to the witness, and therefore I would like to ask to go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can I take you now --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can I take you now to Exhibit number 3160. This is an order by Colonel Obradovic dated the 3rd of July, 1993, and I am referring more specifically to the first item of that order. It's the first page in English and the first page and only page in the B/C/S version. "The civil police of Capljina and Stolac are to take upon themselves and command sweeping authority in terms of protecting the citizens and towns of Capljina and Stolac as well as their property, with a view to preventing looting and violence." Is this the situation how you recall it in the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When it comes to this, as to this kind of security, I didn't feel that on my own skin because I was in the house when three armed soldiers stormed into the house, searched the house looking for gold, jewellery, and money. So I can't say that this was actually the truth of it, that this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to turn to Exhibit 3222. This is again an order by Commander Obradovic dated the 6th of July, 1993. And unless there are objections from the Defence, this is a document that corroborates what has already been explained by the witness, which is the arrest of the Muslim men in fighting age. So I would like to tender the document maybe without putting it again to the witness, as it is something similar to what she already testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd just like to draw your attention the fact that by this order -- this order is a complement to a previous order, so for the Trial Chamber and the completeness of the question asked the witness, it would be necessary to have the previous order, because we don't really know what this present order changes in relation to the previous order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes. But, Counsel Alaburic, during the cross-examination, if you are challenging the contents of the order and its weight, you can present the document that you probably have. That's your work, part of your job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, Your Honour. I just wanted to draw your attention to the fact that here the first point is rescinded of another point in the first order that the Court has no knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. We'll bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness CE, can I take you now to Exhibit number 3222. And more specifically, to the last page -- the second page, last page in the English version, and the second page in the B/C/S version, the paragraph under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Haven't you made a mistake because 3222 is the one we've just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's 3347 indeed. 3347.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the paragraph on page 2 under the title "Security-Related Events." This is a report signed by Kresimir Bogdanovic on the 10th of July, 1993, and it refers to a meeting held at the command company attended by the chief of the military police administration, Mr. Valentin Coric, the commander of the Stolac MUP, Mr. Pero Raguz, and other persons. In your statement, you refer to the chief of MUP, Pero Raguz, who seemed to be in charge of some operations of expulsions on the 4th of August, 1993. Is this the person you refer to in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please? I haven't been able to find my way in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, that was my mistake. The number of the document is 3347, 3347. And the paragraph is on the second page under the title "Security-Related Events." "Sigurnosno", and my B/C/S is not that good. Is this the Pero Raguz that you're referring to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to take you now to Exhibit number 7529?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 7529. In your statement you explained that this certain Dr. Mehmet Kapic was running the Kostana hospital. On the first page of this document, both in the B/C/S and the English version, which is an information by Colonel Siljeg to Colonel Biskic on the 8th of January, 1994. It refers to Dr. Mehmet Kapic that has been arrested by the HVO military police on the occasion of closing down the Stolac field hospital. Is this the Mehmet Kapic you refer to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was a very humane person who worked in the hospital all his life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to take you now to Exhibit 7533.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: And if there is no objection by the Defence, Your Honours, I would like to tender this together with the previous exhibit because it refers exactly to the same document but it has a cover page, and that cover page, of course, cannot be authenticated by the witness, but it is the same content.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can I ask you to go to Exhibit number 9745. Do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is the institution I worked in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kostana hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could I ask you to go to Exhibit number 9746. Do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the VP Dom building where I spent almost four months as a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness CE.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further exhibits and no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As I have already told you, the Defence has one and a half hours at their disposal. I don't know how you've decided to distribute the time, but if I divide the time by six, that makes it 15 minutes per Defence team. So who is going to kick off?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There's a question from the Bench, and I'll give you the floor in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness CE, you spoke about Exhibit number 2215, and you spoke about the order from Colonel Obradovic, who asked that all -- who ordered that all the material and equipment from the osteopathic ward of the hospital should be taken away. Now, I'd like you to tell me whether in that hospital there was just the osteopathy ward or was there another service in the hospital. And why, to the best of your knowledge, all the equipment was taken away?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we just clarify one point. I don't know if it's a matter of the translation, but in point 13, it says that it is ordered to block taking away the equipment from the hospital. So it's not -- the order isn't to take the equipment away but to prevent the equipment from being taken away. There was a ban on taking this away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's another problem here. I don't think the translation of the document is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You're going to help us out here, Mr. Kovacic. You're going to read paragraph 13 out to us in your own language, and with the usual vigilance of the interpreters, they will translate it for us, and that way we'll see clearly how things stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in point 13 of that order, it says as follows: "The commander of the IZM of Stolac should block immediately the entrance of new patients into the Kostana hospital and the taking away of MTS from the hospital, material and technical equipment, MTS." Now, in the translation, these words "taking away the material and technical equipment from the same building" have been translated with the words "Material and technical equipment," whereas in the Croatian, we just have the abbreviation MTS. I don't know where -- this is a draft translation, so not a full version. I don't know where the interpreters get the right to translate the MTS abbreviation with the full words, "material and technical equipment," especially because this abbreviation MTS, in the military jargon, in military jargon, is used for material and technical equipment. That is the abbreviation in military jargon. But here we're dealing with a hospital where the equipment is different and the resources are different. So I don't think that the equipment -- that the translation is the right one because we don't know what the MTS stands for in this particular case. But anyway, it is a ban on taking away MTS regardless of what this MTS stands for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give you the floor, Ms. Egels, but after hearing what has been read out, we have the impression that the order given was to prevent the arrival of new patients to the hospital, to the osteopathic ward of the hospital, and also the order given was to prevent that any material leaves the hospital, which is quite the opposite. It's quite the contrary to the English version as it stands. So what is your position?

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I don't believe it is the contrary to the English version because it says, "Shall immediately block admission of new patients and the taking out of the material." So to my understanding, it blocks both actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, what is much more important is what the witness understood when she said, at page 11, that this is what she remembered from the situation. That paragraph was put to her. The most important thing in the end is what the witness understood, and if she was not under a clear understanding, it must now be re-put it her so we be very clear what the witness said because none of us are giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, counsel. I think this is completely useless because it is so clear what we have, that we should not lose another second on this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, I do not, with respect, agree because we need again -- if it is very clear to the witness, if the witness says, yes, I fully understood when I confirmed this paragraph, then I'm a hundred per cent in agreement with Your Honour. But it may be crystal clear to all of us what's absolutely important in all this and there has been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- that the witness is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Counsel, this, I'm sorry, is a sheer loss of time because there was no misunderstanding. The witness got the text right. We got it right. Those conversant with -- with B/C/S got it right, and there has been a little built of confusion because one Judge understood it in a different way, but it has been shown that that was a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I add this. If a Judge, if one of Your Honours is capable of being momently confused and not understanding, there is a possibility that a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Come on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- witness might also be in the same position. It's important to be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood everything. I understood everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, just a moment. As I didn't understand it myself, could you read paragraph 13 in your own language and give us a comment on that paragraph, paragraph 13. So what is important is your perception of it, and mine as well, because I am completely confused at present. Read paragraph 13 out loud and then you can give us your comments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The commander of the Forward Command Post of Stolac should block the entry of new patients to Kostana hospital and taking out MTS from the hospital, from the same." It is obvious that it is perhaps the terms that are misleading, but I can tell you that I felt all this. I was there. I experienced it when the hospital was evacuated, that nobody was allowed to enter the hospital, and the equipment that was already in the hospital and the equipment that was transported from the Stolac health centre to the hospital could not be taken out, taken away. I hadn't read this piece of paper then, but I was an eyewitness of what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what is described in the text conforms to what you saw, does it, or was it contrary to what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it corresponds to what I saw. It corresponds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have just one question to ask the lady. May we have P 03347 back on our screens. Cross-examination by Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the security related paragraph. 3347 is the document number, and it is the paragraph that is entitled "Security Related," where Mr. Raguz's name is mentioned. I don't want to read it out again. But we can see that a meeting is mentioned there. Tell me, madam, apart from the name of Mr. Pero Raguz, do you know anything else about that meeting? Do you know where it was held, what the topic of discussion was, who was present, or is it only this one name that you recognise from that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just may I take a moment to find my way in the document, please. Do you mean at 1400 hours?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You don't have to read it out loud. Read it to yourself and then we'll hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about this meeting, but on the 4th of August, when I was in front of the ironworks, and I personally know Mr. Pero Raguz --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we know all that. We know that you knew him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I wanted to ask him for a service to do me a service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. All I wanted to hear from you is whether you knew about the meeting, and you didn't. So thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I only have one exhibit. I will be very brief when cross-examining the witness. Could the usher assist me. The exhibit is 2D 272. Can we check to see whether we have it in the e-court system? We have three copies here for the Judges, one for the ELMO and one for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good day, madam. I'd first like to ask you some questions that might reveal your identity, so it might be best to move into private session if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I should just like to start off by asking you to make pauses between my questions and your answer for the interpreters because the interpretation can lag behind and of course they can't be as fast as we are. I just have a brief question. And for that, I would like to have on our screens, P 3160, the document you just a moment ago. May we have the registrar's assistance. I'm sorry, I misspoke. P 01360. Yes, that's the document you were looking at a moment ago. And in connection with that document, you were asked on page 18, line 25 you gave an answer to the question you were asked. I'm not quite clear on the answer, but roughly you said, that when you speak about that document, that you never felt that kind of security on your own skin because you were at home when three soldiers stormed into the house, searched it looking for gold, jewellery, and money. That was your answer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your answer is yes. Right. Now, what I want to ask you is this: When you said that, are you doubting the truthfulness of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I'll rephrase the question. Perhaps I didn't ask it clearly enough. Do you mean by your answer to say that this isn't a true document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me be more precise. Do you mean that a document to that effect was never issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So what you want to say is that the order from this document was not implemented in reality; is that right? In practice, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, then. I will dwell on that document for a moment. From the introductory provision right after the date and also looking at point 1, we can see that the security of the towns of Capljina and Stolac and the property as well should be taken -- that the civil police of Capljina and Stolac are to take it upon themselves and command sweeping authority in terms of protecting the citizens and towns of Capljina and Stolac as well as their property with a view to preventing looting and violence. Did you see that this kind of activity was actually put into practice? Whether they were soldiers or civilians, were they prevented on the ground in engaging in any criminal acts. Did you see that take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to see that. We were in our houses, in our homes, because of the fear we felt in leaving our homes and going outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, the fact that three soldiers did storm your house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you know those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you've already told us that they were looking for valuables in your home; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did they find any valuables? Did they find anything? It's a very simple question. Did they find anything or did they not find anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at that time, I was so afraid that I wasn't an able to register what they were looking for. Yes, they were looking for something. Now, what they took away, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, from what they said and -- was it clear that they were looking for valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your answer is yes, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, counsel. Mr. Praljak next. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, in 1992, in the spring, you lived in Stolac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you in Stolac when the Serb forces entered Stolac with their tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you see anyone -- or, rather, had the Croats fled from the Stolac area prior to that, had they left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were fleeing during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did some Muslims hold flowers in their hands when the tanks entered? Did you see the tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After the arrival of the Serbs, at the end of March and the beginning of April, 1992, did the Serbs and Muslims set up authority in Stolac? Do you know about that, anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So I assume you don't know whether that kind of joint authority existed after the occupation of Sarajevo either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In your statement, which I have before me here, you say that in 1992, during the conflict with the Serbs, the -- the hospital worked normally, functioned normally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But we took in war invalids and the war wounded because the town was shelled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So do you mean the conflict with the Serbs in June when the HVO liberated the area? Is that the conflict you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the statement that we have, your statement, you say that in 1992, during the conflict with the Serbs -- now, are you thinking of June, 1992, when there was fighting between the HVO and the Serb forces for the liberation of Stolac? Is that what you're referring to? When the hospital took in the wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know that the front lines were around Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, I know a lot of things, but what I'm asking you is this: If the Serbs came to Stolac and the Croats pulled out -- or let me start this way: After the liberation of Stolac, as we refer to it, how many Muslims stayed in the Stolac area, in the territory of Stolac? Did a lot of them leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the -- practically, all the Muslims remained.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. They remained. So you don't know the number of Muslims who went to Citluk and Croatia and crossed over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. You don't know anything about that. Thank you. Now, in June, the HVO liberated the Stolac area; is that right? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, nor do I know when that happened exactly, but the fact is that the Serbs withdrew and that the HVO took control of the lines which were lines against the -- defending themselves against the Serbo-Chetnik aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say "withdrew", you say during the conflict with the Serbs, the hospital worked normally, but we took in most of the wounded who were wounded when the town was shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nobody stood still. Of course there were killed and wounded persons too, because there was shooting and shelling. That is normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's leave what is normal. You answer my questions. If there were conflicts, that means that somebody attacked someone else. Do we agree on that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Because there was fighting and you had to get to the lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no -- there was to fighting in town. The Serbs had withdrawn, actually. They had withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. The Serbs had withdrawn just when they -- of their own accord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, whose wounded were in the hospital then? Who came to the hospital and who did you take in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the Serbs withdrew, they -- there was a separation line, a demarcation line, and, of course, some people stayed on. There was -- there were shells falling and people were wounded up at the line and they were brought to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Thank you. You know that very well yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, you do. And you said we received some aid and assistance from outside, but I do know that we received food and medicines from some humanitarian organisations. Tell me this now please: Did you, as a member of the hospital staff, receive any salary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did a single doctor receive a salary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, do you know after that that a brigade was set up of the BH army in the Stolac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the Stolac area, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where was the Bregava Brigade then established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is that Stolac municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Tell me this now, please: Your boyfriend who was in the HVO, did he receive a salary of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He didn't receive a salary either. Right. Now just a couple more questions. You're not a doctor, yourself, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no. No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you ever in Grabovina to see what the hospital looked like there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know how many physicians worked in that particular hospital where these people were transferred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just tell me, you said at one point that your boyfriend, during the month of May in 1993, left and went to liberated territory; is that right? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you until then, was he on occupied territory, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about your -- you, yourself, were you on occupied territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Throughout, during the Serbs and the -- during the HZ HB, you were on occupied territory, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was an occupation of that territory, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you worked there under that occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And your boyfriend was in the occupational army of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That transpired later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know when that transpired. You tell me whether he was in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So if that was occupied territory, the occupying army was the HVO, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So he worked in the occupying army, did he? He was a member of the occupying army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this way --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Go on, then. Explain to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the Serb aggressor withdrew, there were Muslims and Bosniaks in the HVO; no difference between them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean to say Croats and Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Croats and Bosniaks. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the case up to one point when there was something wrong with the situation. You felt there was something wrong with the situation. When what people said didn't hold water, then you felt that something was happening and that's the point in time when he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I didn't deny that. I think that something was afoot. You could feel something in the air. But up until then, was he in the occupying army that had occupied the territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not until that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then he couldn't have moved to liberated territory, could he? Never mind. Tell me this now, please: From the spring of 1992 up until the beginning of the spring and summer of 1993, I think you'll agree with me when I say that there were a lot of Muslims, Bosniaks in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that at Gubavica, we had the Bregava Brigade that was established in October and November of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it existed, but I can't tell you the month.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's fine. Tell me this now, please: Did you in any way whatsoever, because rumours like this were going round, were you aware of a plan of the 4th Corps and commander of the 4th Corps of the BH army by the name of Arif Pasalic, that he was tied in with the Bosniak Muslims who were members of the HVO, and that at a certain point in time, they intended to liberate, if we can put it that way, to liberate Stolac and to take control of the bridges in Capljina and so on? Were you aware of that plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That wasn't something I was aware of or heard about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You didn't hear about that from your boyfriend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were many more beautiful things that we discussed but not that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I do believe you there. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Alaburic, you have 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Madam Witness, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if at all possible, could you give me more time for my cross-examination. As Mr. Kovacic told you, the Defence -- none of the Defence teams, during the consultations we had during the break, will have any questions or, at least, will not have many questions for the next witness, so might I be allowed more time for this witness, because she obviously does have certain knowledge about certain things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say you want more time, how much more do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need another half an hour, which means 45 minutes in total, which would take us up to our next break. I would be very grateful if the Court would accord me that additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we do grant you 45 minutes, but on condition that there are no questions for the following witness. And it is up to the Defence to abide by that. As you know, the Trial Chamber is always flexible, even extremely flexible when it comes to Defence and Defence time. So wherever possible, we try to accord what you have requested. So you're going to have 45 minutes, and as you have a lot of documents to get through, then that is justified on condition that the documents are, of course, relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I myself hope the documents are relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But I'd like to start off by asking you, Witness, something about some documents, documents that you have already seen today and commented on today. So in the Prosecution's sets of documents, would you now take a look at document P 02215. It's an order from commander Nedeljko Obradovic. We have commented on item 13. Is this an order from the commander of the 1st HVO Brigade Knez Domagoj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the signature says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the heading on the first page. Is this the HVO 1st Brigade Knez Domagoj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was this brigade active in the territory of Stolac and in the surroundings? Are you familiar with this name, the Knez Domagoj 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let's have a look at P 03019. That's an order from my client, General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 3019. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You can also have a look at the screen; it might be easier for you. This is an order. Defence department, the chief of the Main Staff of the HVO, my client, General Petkovic, and on the first page of this order above the word "Order", it mentions the addressee. Do you agree that we have the abbreviation OZ JiH here? And you might know that this means the operative zone of South-eastern Herzegovina. So it was an order that was sent to that zone, the area of Mostar, Stolac, and the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, can you confirm that it says that it was sent to that operative zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 2. The commander of that operative zone forwarded the same order to certain brigades. Which brigades did he forward it to? Could you read it out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd HVO Brigade and the 3rd HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let's bear in mind the previous document issued by Nedeljko Obradovic, and we said that the 1st HVO Brigade, the Knez Domagoj Brigade was concerned and would you agree with me that according to this document, this order issued by my client wasn't sent to the first HVO Brigade, it was sent to the 2nd and 3rd HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does the document that you now see show that this order was not forwarded to the 1st HVO Brigade. It was only forwarded to the 2nd and 3rd HVO Brigades.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's go back to the document that concerns the 1st HVO Brigade. 2215 is the number. And just a brief explanation that concerns item 13. This has to do with something that you were asked by my colleague, Senka Nozica. Item 13 is an item we have already read through. It has been interpreted, and it says: "The commander of the Stolac forward command post should block the entry of new patients into the Kostana hospital and should block MTS being taken out, to prevent MTS to be taken out from the hospital." My colleague asked you whether you were suspected of having organised certain activities, for example, taking equipment out of the hospital, and my question is as follows: Are you aware of the fact that in the HVO there were suspicions, according to which, patients were being received in the hospital who were not, in fact, real patients. I'm not asking you whether that's true, but I'm asking you whether you were aware of the fact that this is what some people in the HVO believed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that, within the HVO, they believed that this is how they were augmenting, increasing the number of patients. They were doing this in order to obtain an increasing amount of food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, my comment is the same as yesterday. This is a hypothesis or is this something that is certain, that is supported by documents, because you are telling the witness -- or, rather, you are asking the witness whether there were any rumours according to which the patients or some patients were not in fact real patients, were not in fact sick. Is this a hypothesis or is this something you're certain of? You follow the same procedure when putting questions to the witness and I always feel uneasy because I'm not sure whether we're dealing with speculations or whether what you say is something that is certain. If you say that there were false patients, that means that you have evidence or else you're just coming out with this and waiting to see what the witness will say about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have an order in front us, an order that concerns preventing new patients from entering the hospital and that concerns preventing equipment from being taken out of the hospital. It's quite possible that the author of this order had no factual basis for drafting the sentence that we are now discussing. However, there is another possibility, and that is that the author of this order had certain information or certain suspicions which led him to write the sentence that we are currently discussing. It is my belief that it is my task to determine what is in fact at stake since, as my colleague, Senka Nozica, has also demonstrated, this witness was suspected of having organised certain activities, for example, taking equipment out of the hospital and that is why I'm asking her whether she has any information about such a matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but this is pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If -- if I may, Your Honour. I believe where there is -- where there is good cause to believe, you know, and there is a good faith basis, a question may be posed. So I think perhaps Ms. Alaburic failed to articulate initially what the good faith basis was. Now she's tying it in with Ms. Nozica's questions. Perhaps it's not quite on point, but I believe we should all abide by that rule, that we must have a good faith basis when posing such questions. In other words, something to back up what we are alleging or what is being alleged in a particular question. But I think for the most part, given the earlier answers that we received from Ms. Nozica, there seems to be a good faith basis to suspect that this particular individual, in light of her position, in light of the family members' involvement in certain activities, that there is a good faith basis for Ms. Alaburic to pose these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, so your question is being linked up to the preceding question put by Ms. Nozica. Very well. Do continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in my -- in the first part of the my question, I said that the question was following on the question put by Ms. Nozica, so I think that that was quite clear. And now my last question about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any information according to which certain equipment was taken out of the hospital and, as a result, an order of this kind was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have already said with regard to this document, what I have before me is not something that I have ever seen before, but I was a witness on that day when it was no longer possible for anyone to enter the hospital again and when patients were being evacuated. I was a witness of the time when it was impossible to take things out of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm interested in. What was taken out of the hospital before, and what was it subsequently impossible to take out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing was taken out of the hospital before, but all the medical equipment remained there. That is a fact. And that's what I meant when I said that nothing could be taken out of the hospital. Everything remained there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that on that day you noticed that nothing could be taken out the hospital. Now I would just like know what was being taken out before, since on that day or as of that day, it was no longer possible to take anything out of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we had had certain food supplies at the time and you know what the situation was like in Stolac. Nothing was open. There were no shops that were open, et cetera. So I had the opportunity of taking bread out with me but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps ever take any medical supplies or medicine out with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can now move on to my next series of questions. Witness, in your statement, you mention your father and brother, so could we please now move into private session since I will be mentioning certain names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to ask you something about this report on Mostar. I'll mention the relevant items and sub-items. Item 5A and then 3, pages 5 and 6. It's very simple. You can focus on my question. I'm interested in page 5 and 6 in the B/C/S version, and this is a report for the period from the 27th of June up until the 3rd of July, 1993. And it says that they were very concerned in the HVO about the fact that the Muslims were leading -- leaving the 1st and 3rd HVO brigades and they were joining ABiH units. Tell me, apart from what you have already told us about your boyfriend at the time, do you have any information about other Muslims who left HVO brigades and joined the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's now have a look at the following document: 4698A. It's a SpaBat report again, page 38 in both versions of the document. Only this page has been provided, since this is a very voluminous report. We have recently discussed it, so I think we all still have it in mind. And this report states that what was expected happened at dawn on the 30th of June at 0345 hours. The ABiH launched an attack in the direction of the south, and they took the Tihomir Misic barracks and part of Bijelo Polje to the south-east of the town. It seems that that operation was launched in the night between the 29th and 30th of June when the Muslims, in the ranks of the 3rd Brigade of the HVO, which were based in the Tihomir barracks, in the Tihomir Misic barracks, deserted together with their weapons, in order to join the ABiH. On this occasion, the Muslims advanced towards the north and reached Bijelo Polje. Witness, do you have any information according to which this facility and other areas under HVO control were lost as a result of Muslim betrayal within the HVO ranks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's have a look at 4D 0033. We're in open session. 4D 0033. The 32nd [as interpreted] Mountain Brigade. Do you know which brigade this is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 4th Corps, you know about this too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the 46th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The person who signed it, Haris Huso, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the assessment of the security situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like only to clarify how the interpreter said it was the 46th Brigade, but as far as the document is concerned, before me at least, it is said the 42nd Brigade. So that is the document 4D 00033. Isn't it so? So it is now the 42nd or 46th?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about the 42nd Brigade. I wasn't following the transcript, so I didn't notice a mistake. So we're talking about 42nd Brigade in the lower part of the text, third and fourth lines from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says: "Use the civilian authorities to establish contact with all members of the Muslim population and request that they become fully engaged in defending their homes." And the next task: "Appeal to all Muslims who are members of the HVO to place themselves at the disposal of their people." Witness, are you aware of any activities that had been undertaken to attain these objectives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My colleague mentions that the date of the document hasn't been mentioned, so I'll repeat what I said. The 16th of April, 1993, is the date. Now let's move on to the next document 4D 00034. It is a document by the same author, the chief of security of the 42nd Mountain Brigade two days later, or, rather, the 18th of April, 1993. And I'm going to read out the fifth bullet point, the third and fifth bullet points and the task are as follows: "Through the organs of the civilian authorities, to establish cooperation with the inhabitants of Dubrava and Stolac." This is a more precise assignment now. And next, the third bullet point: "To establish cooperation with our fighters in the HVO and indicate the seriousness of the situation to them." Do you have any knowledge about these activities of the BH army to link up with the Muslims in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about any of this. It would appear that I was engaged militarily and not a health worker. I don't know why you're asking me any of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you, because you deserve an answer to why I'm asking you this question. With the Court's permission, I'll tell the witness. I'm asking you this question because the Prosecutor showed you a military document earlier on and wanted to introduce the document through you into evidence. Now, the author of this document is my client, General Petkovic. So what I want to do through my questions now is to show the following: First of all, whether the order reached the brigade which was active in the area you were in; and secondly, to establish why the order was issued. And I think that it -- regardless of what went on, that you have the right to know why an order was written, regardless of what you think about that order and whether it brought any difficulties to your life. I simply feel that you have the right to know what the factual basis was for a order of this kind to be issued.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: These are not documents that we are looking at for the first time in this courtroom. So let's take a look at the next document together. It is 4D 00035, and it is a document by the commander of the 42nd Mountain Brigade this time, (redacted). Does the name (redacted) sounds familiar?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's do our best not -- do our best to avoid pinpointing whether you were anybody's neighbour, who was your neighbour. But what I wanted to ask you about was the last line of point 3. "The morale -- prepare the personnel to --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat what she's reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Alaburic, would you repeat that portion that you just read out, the last point of point 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The organ for moral affairs, the IPD and VP, information propaganda religious affairs, will draft a plan for informing the personnel, the members of the brigade, the inhabitants of Mostar, Capljina, and Stolac municipalities, and the Muslim soldiers in the HVO Croatian Defence Council units in these municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, my question to you was as follows: Do you have any knowledge of the fact that the BH army would inform the members of the Muslim ethnic group in the ranks of the HVO what they should do and how they should act and be prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us now look at another document to which General Praljak referred when he asked you his questions, and it is number 4D 00036, the following document. This time it is a level even higher up. It is the 4th Corps commander. And do you know who the 4th Corps commander was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It was Arif Pasalic. Have you ever heard of the name Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at what he says in the report to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces, what he wrote on the 2nd of May, 1993. And let's us focus on point 3, the second paragraph, and I quote: "Tying up has been affected with our people in the HVO." And further on in point 3, it goes on to say that the men from the Capljina HVO have the task of taking Tasovcici village and the bridge in Capljina in order to prevent troops from being brought in from the direction of Metkovic. And then there are other assignments, too, intended for the members of the Muslim ethnic group within HVO ranks. Now, tell me, please, did you have any knowledge about any of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm told to draw your attention to something else. Just a moment, please. May I just take a moment to find it. Let us take a look at where it says: "Take control of the town of Stolac with our men in the HVO." Now, since you are from Stolac, I have been warned that we should clarify this situation. So were you informed about the task whereby the Muslims in the HVO, precisely in Stolac, tied in with the BH army, should in fact take control of the town of Stolac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Happy to. Were you informed in any way that members of the Muslim ethnic group within the HVO had the order of taking -- or seizing -- or seizing Stolac from the HVO and handing it over to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You don't. Right. Now let us take a look, but before we do so, let me tell you that when we discussed these documents with members of UNPROFOR, it was stated that this kind of conduct by the members of one ethnic group, desertion of this kind, is considered high treason in any army. So I'm asking you for your opinion. And if the Court allows me and if you agree, would you say this was high treason? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, is it normal, as far as you're concerned, that the members of an army should act in this way? All right. I take that question back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a question that perhaps goes above the witness's head because it is a legal issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I -- if I may, Your Honour. Perhaps by using the technical word, the legal term, yes. However, the content itself could be asked of the witness, especially since the witness's testimony on direct examination. You know, so if she was aware of this activity and what this activity, if indeed it was occurring, how it might be perceived by the other people. If we phrase it that way, it takes away the technical term, the term of art treason and allows the witness to give us her opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I really -- I wouldn't like to enter into a debate on technical legal terms, but I do feel that the witness is here. She is not an expert in military matters in the first case. In the second, she is of course even less an expert on legal issues and kind of high treason and everything else which had been asked for from her. So therefore, I would also ask Counsel Alaburic probably not to formulate questions which are really beyond the competence and the knowledge of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may. If I may add a point. I really cannot see in any way how the opinion of this witness on such a question could be of any use to the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, since I raised that issue. See, here is the conundrum, Your Honour. By using this technique -- you see, we're asked to respond to the Prosecution's technique. They are bringing in documents which the witness is absolutely clueless about and they're asking her to comment in a rather leading fashion, yes or no. And that forces us now to use other documents because this tests the witness's knowledge and activities at the time and place. If she is saying simply on direct, "Well, this is what the bad Croats were doing," and now we're showing that here is some other evidence that you'll perhaps -- at the other side was engaging in certain activity, she can say I don't know, I'm not aware of it. Had you been aware of this, would this change your opinion? I think this is perfectly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I'm objecting to her giving an evaluation. Do you think this is such a crime or this is good or this is bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would agree with you on that. But if she were to be asked, with all due respect, do you think this activity was ongoing, might this activity cause some concerns which would lead him to, for instance, search for weapons, carry out other activities. And I think that's where Ms. Alaburic is going to. She's merely responding to the direct examination and, frankly, I must say, you know I fully support what is going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to add my point of view on this matter. The problem as far as the Defence is concerned is to put into evidence the fact that the members of the HVO, who were Muslims, left the HVO at a precise point in time, and that by leaving the HVO, from the point of view of the Defence, legally speaking, this could be qualified as being high treason. All right. That's what the Defence wishes to show. Now, you can ask this type of question of a military witness. We're going to have officers, HVO officers come in to testify, BH army officers. So that's the kind of question you can ask them and people who are in the know, whereas the witness here is a nurse. So to ask her -- you would have to ask her about the hospital, about illnesses, about injections and things like that. You're asking her questions about high treason. Well, why not ultimately, but what weight is her answer going to carry? It is quite obvious that if you asked the same question of an officer, that would be far more interesting as far as the Court was concerned. I give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Thank you -- thank you, Your Honour. Just for the record, indeed, this is irrelevant and speculation. The witness answered the question of the Defence as to if she knew or didn't know about the activities of her husband in 1992. The witness answered the question to the Defence as to whether or not her husband left the HVO at one point. For the rest, this witness is not the one who should be asked anything further on the question of what is it qualified and what is her opinion about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just observe that my lead counsel took the question back at 11.49, since when we stood her and said nothing at all. It's --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I be allowed to explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I'll deal with the problem. Witness, your boyfriend, who later became your husband, left the HVO, and nobody is challenging that. That seems to be accepted. While he was -- you might have had some conversations with him. Now, when you were talking together intimately, did you look into the possibility of his leaving the HVO being considered by some legal authority as -- as possible treason or high treason? In your conversations with him, did you ever raise that matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. But let me tell you, when he left in May, we were in the hospital the whole time. We wouldn't leave at all. We would be given one or two days to rest during one month, but we were there round the clock, 24 hours. We had no contacts with anybody. We worked there. We were there when the shells were falling. The population had moved quite a bit due to the shelling. They went to Capljina, to Pocitelj, or towards the coast. So that from the month of May right up to when I was released from prison, I had absolutely no contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Can we just clarify one point? We didn't know up until this time when your boyfriend of the time left the HVO and joined the BH army. You've now told us that took place in May, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I didn't see him after that, after that date, but when he left, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said that he went in May. You didn't give us the year, but we know that we're dealing with 1993. So was it May, 1993, when you were answering the question by His Honour Judge Antonetti? Were you telling the truth that he left in May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And May, 1993, did that follow on from all the orders that I've just read out to you that were dated April, 1993, including the one by Arif Pasalic in May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did that happen after all these orders were issued, the ones that I read out to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Egels.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, speculation. She just said that she has not seen her boyfriend after he left, so how would she know why he left?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say to my learned colleague, we're not dealing with the reasons he left, but the fact of his leaving at that particular date, leaving the HVO. And in response to His Honour's question, the witness herself said it was May, 1993, and my question was along the lines of noting that that was after all these orders had been issued, the ones I read out a moment ago. And of course May comes after April, so there is no dilemma on that score. I have no separate questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry again, Ms. Alaburic, but, frankly, I do not understand. The witness is here -- is here, but she is not here for being a witness about her boyfriend and later her husband. She's here to be a witness about those -- those events which happened in 1992, 1993, and especially when it was related -- those events which were related to her presence in the hospital, et cetera. So I understand the situation and I understand your reasons and the others' reasons to speak about her boyfriend and husband, but really, I do not see the very close relationship between her being here as a witness and -- and her boyfriend and husband on the other hand. So I'm sorry, but I would like to say that probably the questions might be put in an another way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, the problem is that we don't understand your strategy. We don't understand what you wish to demonstrate. Perhaps, with a more concise question, you will be able to explain to us what it is you wish to show, because all the Judges have said this. First of all, she's not a military person. Secondly, she always answers no to anything asked about military documents. My colleagues have brought this up and told you that, yes, her boyfriend was her boyfriend, but she was in the hospital at the time and that she can't add to anything she's already said. So what do you wish to demonstrate? I really -- I'm not following your argument. And if we don't understand it, then it's wasted time for everyone, for you who have spent a lot of time preparing your cross-examination, but for justice as well, in general terms. So try and ask precise, concise questions to show what you're trying to demonstrate. All I'm asking is to be able to understand, but in order to do so, you have to explain it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I'd like to provide you with two explanations before I explain my question. I'd like to tell Judge Prandler that I believe it's not fair if one objects to the Defence for having put questions to the witness about certain military documents, since the examination-in-chief was based on military documents, and if the Chamber had objected to the Prosecution in the same way, I wouldn't have had the idea of showing this witness a single document. And the second thing is that I must admit that I expected the Trial Chamber to intervene in this manner, and I was wondering about how I should respond to such an objection, and I think that it would also be good to remind you of certain other war events. For example, what happened in the USA, when the war with Japan broke out, what happened to the Japanese citizens of the USA -- to the Japanese who were citizens of the USA, what happened -- anti-terroristic measures that violate human rights. For example, in the USA, Great Britain, France, measures that discriminate against the Muslims, discriminate against people who have an Arab appearance and can be identified as Muslims. We're talking about certain measures that at certain points in time may seem to be discriminatory. And the question is: Are these measures justified or not? I know that the order issued by my client, that we are now discussing, is one of the key orders that concern his responsibility, and I believe that it is my duty to show the factual basis for issuing that order. If -- it's not disputed that many Muslims left the HVO and joined the ABiH in a way that could be considered to be treason, and if they left with their weapons, if they were linked up for months, and if in a certain sense, they were in reserve at HVO positions, they were being kept in reserve in HVO positions at a given point in time, they disarmed HVO members and surrendered the positions to the ABiH, well, I believe in that case, it is the responsibility of any military commander to take the necessary measures. I believe that this is what my client in fact did. And I would like to continue analysing this order because we can see how the civilian population, women and children, were to be treated, et cetera. That's the only reason. As far as the questions put to this witness are concerned, I'd like to say the following: This witness has shown an understanding of the situation at the time, and the positions about the situation at the time. The witness hasn't said that her boyfriend left the HVO. She said that he was free to reach the liberated territory. And these are the reasons for which I have been putting these questions to the witness. I don't know whether it's time to have the break now or whether we should conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Do try to conclude your cross-examination. Mr. Registrar, how much time has Ms. Alaburic used up so far? We've given you some time. We've said three-quarters of an hour, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, there is just one other document I would like to have a look at.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another criminal report, Witness. It's in my bundle of documents under number 4D -- I apologise. P 06916.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Since I'll be mentioning names again, could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we call the witness into the courtroom, the Chamber will now read out an oral decision. I will read it out slowly that the interpreters, who have been provided with a copy of the decision, can interpret. Decision on the request for certification of the motion to appeal the Chamber's decision of the 13th of November, 2006, on adoption of new measures to bring the trial to an end within a reasonable time. On the 13th of November, 2006, the Chamber rendered a decision, hereinafter, the contested decision, on the adoption of new measures to bring the trial to an end within a reasonable time, a decision in which, among other things, it reduced by 107 hours the amount of time granted to the Prosecution to present its case. On the 20th of November, 2006, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting the certification of the motion to appeal the contested decision pursuant to Rule 73(B) and 73(C) of the Rules. On the same day, the Petkovic Defence also filed a motion requesting the certification of the motion to appeal the contested decision, but this only concerned reducing by 107 hours the amount of time granted to the Prosecution for the presentation of its case. On the 22nd of November, the other accused expressed their support for the motion filed by the accused Petkovic. The Chamber must rule on the conditions under which 73 bis of the Rules of Procedure are applicable -- is applicable. It's not 73 bis. The Rule concerned is 73(B). The Chamber notes that the Defence is only indirectly concerned by the decision to reduce by 107 hours the time granted to the Prosecution. In fact -- or, firstly, the contested decision does not determine the mode followed by the Defence and the time allocated to the Defence to present its case. Secondly, although reducing the amount of time allocated for the examination-in-chief would result in reducing the total amount of time allocated for the cross-examination, such reduction will not affect the fairness or expeditious conduct of the proceedings pursuant to Rule 73(B) of the Rules. The reduction of the time granted for cross-examination is a reduction proportional to the reduction of time granted for the examination-in-chief, which does not affect the right of the accused to cross-examine Prosecution witnesses. The accused will, in fact, have the necessary amount of time available for cross-examination. In this respect, the Chamber notes that it determines the amount of time to be allocated for the cross-examination on a case-by-case basis after having examined, on the basis of the previously given witness statement, the anticipated scope of the witness's testimony. To the extent that the Chamber has allowed and will continue to allow more frequent recourse to the procedure provided for under Rule 92 ter of the Rules, the Chamber will continue to ensure that the accused have at their disposal a sufficient amount of time for cross-examination. The Chamber has, in fact, always allocated significantly more time to the Defence for their cross-examination of witnesses called pursuant to Rule 92 ter. In conclusion, a proportional reduction of the time allocated for cross-examination will not significantly affect the fairness or expeditiousness of the proceedings nor their outcome. The Chamber, however, grants the Prosecution motion, the Prosecution being directly concerned by the contested decision. The reduction of the amount of time allocated for the Prosecution case could, in its opinion, significantly compromise the fairness and, in particular, the expeditiousness of the proceedings. As the Chamber has stated in paragraph 14 of the contested decision, the question as to what constitutes reasonable time constitutes a question that concerns fairness and the expeditiousness of the proceedings pursuant to Rule 20 and 21 of the Statute. Given that an immediate decision by the Appeals Chamber could help to expedite the proceedings, the Chamber hereby grants the Prosecution motion and decides to certify the appeal. For the foregoing reasons, the Chamber hereby rejects the Defence motion, grants the Prosecution motion, and certifies the appeal of the contested decision.
